title: Cohort Router: quota-aware spillover with soft-preempt and model-sibling promotion
creator: Nina Rodriguez
description: Design and implement a cohort-based routing component that prioritizes requests by plan tier (free, paid, enterprise), applies quota-aware soft preemption windows, and promotes compatible fallback model variants when the primary tier or region is constrained.
background: Current tier routing is largely deterministic: requests are mapped to plan lanes and rejected or deferred when quotas exhaust. We lack a coherent spillover strategy that preserves enterprise SLOs while providing degraded service for free users. Teams have requested: graceful demotion instead of hard reject, regional affinity to reduce cross-region latency, and a systematic way to prefer model-variant fallbacks (smaller quantized variants or cached responses) under contention.
goals: 1) Prevent hard rejects for payers where possible; 2) Maintain enterprise latency SLOs by preempting lower-priority cohorts in soft windows; 3) Route to regional capacity first and fall back to model-variants before global failovers; 4) Expose policy knobs and observability for incident analysis.
non_goals: Do not change billing calculus or long-term quota definitions; not implementing per-tenant ML-based prioritization in this scope (future work).
proposed_solution: Introduce a Cohort Router service sitting in front of the admission controller. Key features: 1) Cohort buckets: free/paid/enterprise with token budgets and sliding-window usage. 2) Soft-preempt windows: short (100-500ms) time windows where lower cohorts are nudged to slower lanes or cheaper model variants rather than forcibly evicted. 3) Spillover policies: tier-aware thresholds trigger promotion of fallback variants (e.g., fp16 quantized model, smaller context window, cached prefix responses) with an ordered fallback matrix per model. 4) Regional affinity scoring: prefer same-region placement; if region capacity < threshold, attempt cross-region vs model-variant based on latency risk. 5) Transparent decision logging and per-request tags for Console and tracing.
config_parameters:
- cohort_weights: {free:0.2, paid:0.5, enterprise:0.3}
- soft_preempt_window_ms: 250
- heap_reserve_ratio: 0.12
- fallback_matrix: [primary->quant_8bit, primary->fp16_small, primary->cached_prefix, primary->fallback-api]
- regional_capacity_threshold_pct: 60
- promotion_latency_budget_ms: 30
api_changes: Add 'cohort_hint' optional header to inference API and include 'routing_decision' field in response metadata. Admin console exposes per-cohort knobs and on/off toggle for soft-preempt mode.
data_migration: No persistent migration required. Cohort Router reads plan tier and quota state from existing quota service; we will add a light-weight cache for sliding-window counters with TTL to avoid blast to quota DB.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged dev rollout to internal staging with synthetic traffic (2 days). 2) Canary enabling for 5% of traffic on staging-1 region (3 days). 3) Gradual ramp on hosted region US-WEST over 7 days with detailed SLO monitoring. 4) Enable global but keep soft-preempt disabled by default for 2 weeks, then opt-in by account for paid customers. 5) After confidence, enable default for free cohort with stricter fallbacks.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: cohort_admits, cohort_demotions, fallback_promotions, regional_spillovers, average_decision_latency. Alerts: spike in cohort_demotions > 5x baseline for 10m, fallback_promotions rate > 10% for enterprise, decision_latency_p50 > 50ms. Dashboards: per-region/per-tier heatmap and per-model fallback waterfall.
acceptance_criteria: Router honors cohort weights and reduces hard rejects by 90% for paid tier under simulated 2x load.
Enterprise latency p95 remains within SLA when paid/free cohorts experience overload and soft-preempt is active.
Fallback promotion trace shows ordered fallbacks and a per-request routing_decision recorded in logs.
Admin console exposes controls for soft_preempt_window_ms and fallback_matrix and changes apply without restart.
Security review completed and KMS access patterns unchanged.
implementation_tasks: Design Cohort Router proto and decision API (backend + SDK changes).
Implement sliding-window counter cache with eviction and TTL.
Add fallback matrix engine with model-variant metadata mapping.
Integrate regional capacity scorer and cross-region latency estimator.
Wire routing_decision metadata into tracing and Console.
Add admin UI knobs and feature flag.
Run performance tests and chaos scenarios (Simulate region outage, token surge).
Complete security review and update threat model.
risks_mitigations: Risk: promotion to cheaper model variants may degrade quality and trigger customer complaints. Mitigation: per-model QA thresholds and automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed threshold; start with conservative fallbacks for enterprise. Risk: added decision latency. Mitigation: keep router decision path <5ms and offload expensive checks to async evaluators.
notes: Design reviewed with PM (Arjun Mehta) on 2026-02-28; PM requested explicit console visibility for customers.
Related research: perf tests for quantized variants in runtime-1.22 showed 2.3x throughput improvement but 3-5% BLEU/acc drift for specific tasks.
